articleTitle: Optical Fiber Sources Design in OptiSystem Software
abstract: OptiSystem software is a tool that is well suited for conducting numerical simulations for designing fiber lasers. Novel pumping scheme for holmium-doped fiber amplifier (HDFA) using commercially available 980nm and 1480nm laser diodes is proposed using cascaded fiber lasers. The first fiber laser uses erbium-doped fiber to generate a continuous-wave (CW) laser at 1620nm, while the second fiber laser uses thulium-doped fiber to generate a CW laser at 1950nm, which is used to pump the HDFA.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency On-Chip Antenna on a Silicon Photonics Platform
abstract: This paper reports on the design, simulation, and fabrication of two on-chip antennas, the triangular patch antenna, and the blade antenna, on a commercial silicon photonics technology platform. Implementing on-chip antennas will help to reach high-speed inter- and intra-chip communication between and within photonic integrated circuits.

articleTitle: On-Chip Loop-Terminated Mach-Zehnder Interferometer Gas Sensor
abstract: On-chip gas sensor using widespread silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technology is presented. The design is based on loop-terminated Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (LT-MZI) which enhance the sensor performance by a factor of two as compared to conventional MZI. Slot waveguide is used to further increase the sensitivity of the gas sensor. Finite difference eigenmode (FDE) solver and finite difference time domain (FDTD) solver were used to optimize and obtain the sensor performance. A figure of merit (FOM) of 230 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is achieved with interferometer arms of only 100 µm.

articleTitle: Mechanically Actuated Asymmetric Slab Waveguide: Optical and Mechanical Design Considerations
abstract: Multiphysics numerical simulations have been performed to investigate how the trapezoid geometry affects the mechanical and optical properties of deforming slab waveguides.

articleTitle: Analysis of time-delay photonic reservoirs for neuromorphic computing
abstract: We numerically investigate time-delay photonic reservoirs to provide a deep understanding of their complex nonlinear dynamics, in connection to their memory and performance to solve machine learning problems. We explore the ability of such systems to tackle tasks with progressing difficulty towards optimized neuromorphic photonic applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of full-field super-resolution terahertz imaging using a microbolometric camera
abstract: We report on the investigation of a super-resolution imaging technique for terahertz waves using a terahertz camera. The technique we used, called super-resolution orthogonal deterministic imaging, was performed with a microbolometer terahertz camera allowing quasi-real time reconstruction of highly resolved near-field images.

articleTitle: Direct and Externally Modulated Fabry-Perot Laser for THz Bandwidth Frequency Comb Generation
abstract: We report a direct and externally modulated Fabry-Perot laser based frequency comb of bandwidth ≈1.33 THz and flatness less than 6 dB. The measured RIN of the lines from DC to 15 GHz on an average is about -150 dBc/Hz and the linewidth of about 5 MHz.

articleTitle: Dielectric Nanoantennas – Enhanced Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance for Sensing Applications
abstract: A subwavelength bridge between free-space optical radiation and localized electromagnetic energy is formed by an optical antenna. Its geometries and material composition have a major influence on its localized electromagnetic modes. Here, the design of silicon-based plasmonic nanoantennas is proposed and numerically analyzed. In comparison to plasmonic nanoantennas, high-index dielectric nanoantennas exhibit several advantages such as CMOS compatibility and low ohmic losses that may benefit nanophotonic applications. The surrounding material affects the enhanced localized field as well as the wavelength of the enhancement peak. In this work, the dipole nanoantenna is proposed with a silicon material of large excess carrier concentrations. The enhancement occurs in the mid-IR spectral region and it is useful for sensing and biochemical applications.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Stimulated Raman Microscopy Images using a 1D Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Stimulated Raman Scattering (SRS) microscopy is a powerful nonlinear optical imaging technique deriving contrast from Raman active molecular vibrations. We demonstrate, using a supervised convolutional neural network (RM-Net), the creation of chemical maps from hyperspectral Stimulated Raman Scattering images. Using a limited number (800) of training spectra, the trained RM-Net model was successfully applied to new hyperspectral images without compromising accuracy.

articleTitle: Low-Threshold Pulley-Coupled Thulium-Silicon Microdisk Lasers
abstract: In this work, we present low-threshold lasing in compact thulium-silicon hybrid microdisk resonators with a pulley-coupled design. We observe total on-chip output powers of more than 2 mW and threshold pump powers of < 1 mW.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction for Low Data Regimes in Photonics Design
abstract: Efficient exploration of high-dimensional parameter space is essential in modern photonic component design. Linear dimensionality reduction such as principal component analysis has proven useful in identifying lower dimensional subspace of interest in several design problems. Yet such subspaces often exhibit curvature reflecting nonlinear relationships between design parameters. For such systems linear dimensionality reduction methods can be suboptimal. We discuss how an appropriate architecture for an autoencoder neural network along with a numerically robust initialization, show improved performance compared to linear methods even in low data regimes, which are typical for photonic design problems.

articleTitle: Efficient Waveguide Taper Design with Rapid and Data-Driven Eigenmode Expansion
abstract: A novel, highly flexible, and data-driven method for designing compact and efficient integrated optical tapers will be discussed and demonstrated through state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Highly-efficient subwavelength grating metamaterial antenna for silicon waveguides
abstract: We present a high-efficient silicon-based surface grating antenna in a 300-nm silicon-on-insulator platform. The antenna comprises metamaterial engineered L-shaped radiating nanostructures, and has a design efficiency of 89% and a compact footprint of 7.6 µm × 4.5 µm.

articleTitle: Deterministic single-photon subtraction based on bi-exciton transitions of a quantum dot
abstract: We propose and numerically simulate a scheme for deterministic subtraction of a single photon from an arbitrary pulse of light. The scheme relies on the bi-exciton transitions in a quantum dot forming a Λ-system, while each transition is coupled to a different mode of a bi-modal nano-cavity.

articleTitle: Progress on Silicon Photonic Thermometry for Secondary and Working Measurement Standards
abstract: Silicon photonic thermometers are candidates for next generation secondary and working thermometry standards. We report on recent progress at NRC on Si ring resonator thermometers. The thermometer module uses non-contact stress free assembly, and free space optical coupling to the ring from a multi-fiber block. A temperature measurement reproducibility of better than ±5 mK over hundreds of hours has been achieved by using improved ring design, SiO2 cladding materials, and low optical power to avoid self-heating. These results represent an order of magnitude improvement over previous work.

articleTitle: Time-domain topology optimization of wideband dispersive plasmonic nanostructures
abstract: We present a time-domain topology optimization algorithm to inverse design dispersive materials based on the Drude model. The method is demonstrated on plasmonic nanostructures with wideband performance.

articleTitle: Towards transform-limited single photons from a nanowire quantum dot
abstract: Quantum dots embedded within different photonic structures can generate single photons and entangled photon pairs efficiently and at high emission rates. We present a single photon source based on a quantum dot embedded within a nanowire waveguide fabricated using selective-area vapour-liquid-solid epitaxy. The device generates single photons at a high repetition rate limited by the quantum dot lifetime (τ ~ 1 ns) and with low multi-photon emission probability (g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(0) ~ 0). Furthermore, linewidths of the emitted photons approach the Fourier-transform limit when the sources are excited above-band.

articleTitle: Machine learning for performance homogeneity of photonic chips
abstract: The performance homogeneity of photonic chips is critical when it comes to the deployment of the technology in high volume applications. We present our research for using machine learning for optimization of the design space and prediction of optical performance of the planar lighwave circuit technology in volume manufacturing.

articleTitle: Purification at the ultimate limit using quantum superpositions of causal order
abstract: Pure states are essential to quantum technologies. We show how generate an unlimited number of pure states by applying a pair of operations in a superposition of their causal order.

articleTitle: Surface Plasmon Polariton Excitation Based on Refractive Index Tunable Technique
abstract: A novel phase matching idea of surface plasmon polariton (SPP) design is presented based on changing of the prism refractive index in Kretschmann configuration. The selected prism material is a thermotropic liquid crystalline material (TLC) which has been chemically prepared in vitro and was thermally and optically characterized. The experimentally measured refractive indices of the LC material possess a linear change with the temperature at several selected wavelengths in the visible region. The resonant excitation of the SPP was theoretically confirmed by the thermal control of the prism refractive index and can be utilized in analyte refractive index sensing.

articleTitle: Athermal and Tunable Si-Photonic MZI-Echelle Grating Wavelength Demultiplexers
abstract: The temperature induced channel wavelength shift in WDM components must be corrected by either active temperature control, active on-chip tuning, or if possible, the use of intrinsically athermal devices. Experimental results are presented for three silicon photonic echelle grating demultiplexers that use a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) to launch light into the echelle device. The temperature induced shifts of the MZI-echelle channel wavelengths are suppressed (athermal) or enhanced (super-thermal), or the channel wavelengths are actively tuned by an on-chip micro-heater. The super-thermal and micro-heater configurations allow channel wavelength tuning with lower tuning power than full chip temperature control.

articleTitle: Water Quality Measurement using Plasmonic Fiber-Optic Sensors with Alternative Materials
abstract: We propose a plasmonic fiber-optic sensor for measuring various water characteristics based on surface plasmon resonance at the interface between nanoparticles and water. Instead of using conventional plasmonic materials like gold and silver, we utilized transition metal nitrides as the plasmonic nanofilms. We examined the sensing performance of the proposed sensor by depositing the nanofilms on a polished region of the optical fiber and using a broadband light source and a detector.

articleTitle: Terahertz polarization-division multiplexing within a four-wire waveguide
abstract: We demonstrate a new metal-wire waveguide topology, namely a four-wire waveguide, which simultaneously acts as a broadband terahertz polarization-division multiplexer and as a novel platform to realize the independent manipulation of polarization-division multiplexed terahertz signals.

articleTitle: Quantitative Phase Microscopy with Ultra-high Sensitivity for Profiling Single-layer Materials
abstract: We propose an ultra-high sensitivity quantitative phase microscopy method for profiling single-layer material structures. Our method relies on a high sensitivity detection scheme, implementing common-path interferometry and high full-well-capacity camera, and an accurate thickness retrieval algorithm, derived from a transmission matrix model. We applied our system for profiling 2D materials, e.g., monolayer MoS2, and validated the results with conventional methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Transverse-Mode Optical Processors: Towards On-chip Programming and Calibration
abstract: We design a Multi-Transverse-Mode Optical Processor (MTMOP) exploiting the first two quasi-transverse electric modes (TE0 and TE1). This design enables the on-chip measurement of optical phase required for programming the optical processors.

articleTitle: Si-Photonic Waveguide Grating Coupler Arrays for Wavefront Monitoring
abstract: A silicon photonic wavefront monitoring chip may be designed using arrays of surface grating couplers. Such a chip can monitor wavefront distortion across a pupil plane in adaptive optics systems for free space optical communications and astronomy. This paper reports experimental results for grating pair wavefront monitor elements intended as building blocks for such an array. Wavefront tilt signals of 6 dB/degree and 10 dB/degree, respectively, are measured for grating pairs arranged in power ratio and interferometric configurations.

articleTitle: SiN/SOI Sub-dB Butt-Coupling Scheme in the O-Band
abstract: The monolithic integration of micro-metric silicon nitride and silicon-on-insulator platforms is presented. We demonstrate an interconnection of sub-dB coupling loss and less than -16dB back-reflection for operation in the O-band.

articleTitle: AlGaN Deep UV LEDs on Si Exploiting a Nanowire-assisted AlN Buffer Layer
abstract: In this paper, we report AlGaN deep UV LEDs emitting down to 247 nm made with AlGaN epilayers using a special AlN buffer layer on Si substrate.

articleTitle: Guiding Light in Water-Filled Hollow-Core Photonic-Bandgap Fibers
abstract: We study the guiding of visible and near-infrared light through 800nm and 1550nm hollow-core photonic-bandgap fibers filled with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O with the goal of using the fibers for probing of and enhanced light collection from water-based samples. We observe that selective filling only the fiber core maintains the spectral range of the fiber while filling both the hollow core and the photonic crystal cladding results in a frequency shift of the photonic bandgap due to the resulting refractive index change.

articleTitle: Hilbert-Schmidt speed-based witness faithfully detects non-Markovianity
abstract: Hilbert-Schmidt speed (HSS)-based witness, a quantifier of quantum statistical speed having the advantage of avoiding the diagonalization of the evolved density matrix, has been introduced as a trustful witness of non-Markovianity in low-dimensional systems. We investigate the sensitivity of this HSS-based witness to detect non-Markovianity in high-dimensional and multipartite open quantum systems. We find that the time behaviors of the HSS-based witness are always in agreement with those of quantum negativity or quantum correlation measures. These results show that the HSS-based witness is a faithful identifier of the memory effects appearing in the quantum evolution of a high-dimensional system.

articleTitle: In situ training with silicon photonics neural networks
abstract: Deep learning hardware accelerators based on analog photonic networks are trained on standard digital electronics. We discuss on-chip training of neural networks enabled by a silicon photonic architecture for parallel, efficient, and fast data operations.

articleTitle: Compressed Ultrafast Tomographic Imaging
abstract: We have developed compressed ultrafast tomographic imaging (CUTI), which passively records two-dimensional transient events with a standard streak camera. CUTI is exhibited as a new imaging mode universally adaptable to most streak cameras.

articleTitle: Ultra-compact multistage interferometric devices for optical communication
abstract: Densification of photonic functionality is important as the optical communication industry strives to achieve higher levels of integration. We present a new approach for folding multistage interferometric devices such that waveguide density reaches its theoretical limit. The feasibility of the approach is validated by a demonstration of a CWDM multiplexer, which was realized in a silica-on-silicon platform in a footprint of 0.18 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and exhibits state-of-the-art optical performance characteristics.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Prediction of Fabrication Variations in Silicon Photonic Devices
abstract: Next-generation silicon photonic devices often contain complex, nanoscale features to enhance their performance; however, these features experience significant variations from fabrication imperfections, which cause significant performance degradation in practical implementation. We present a machine learning model that learns from a modest set of scanning electron microscope images to quickly and accurately predict the fabrication variations. Additionally, we present the potential use of this model in the automated correction of fabrication-sensitive device features.

articleTitle: SrTiO3, a near-field terahertz sensor
abstract: Nonlinear optics at spatially resolved terahertz (THz) frequencies under diffraction remains an almost unexplored field. We report here the performance of a bulk SrTiO3 (STO) crystal as a near-field sensor using a combination of a high-field terahertz source and a two-dimensional imaging capability. Thanks to the Kerr effect detection of THz waves, the STO sensor outperforms current Pockels effect-based near-field THz sensors. Furthermore, its ability to remain polarized for several picoseconds could pave the way for a new strategy to build an ultrafast space-time THz memory.

articleTitle: Photonic Cavities in the Far-UVC with Point Defects in Bottom-up Nanowire Photonic Crystals
abstract: In this paper, we propose photonic cavities in the far-ultraviolet (UV)-C band using point defects in bottom-up AlGaN nanowire photonic crystals.

articleTitle: Generation of High-Order Vortex States from Two-Mode Photon-Number Squeezed States
abstract: We report a scheme for generation of quadrature vortex states using two-mode squeezed states. Our scheme has the potential to improve measurement sensitivity for applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

articleTitle: Comparison of near-infrared and mid-infrared link budgets for optical satellite communication
abstract: Link budgets for LEO to ground optical communication using state of the art MWIR and LWIR sources and detectors were generated using OptiWave’s OptiSystem simulation suite. The results show a MWIR link demonstration could be viable in the next 5 years, while LWIR links are limited by detector technology. MWIR and LWIR sources and detectors using nonlinear optics are discussed.

articleTitle: Meander Antenna on a Photonics Chip
abstract: We experimentally characterize an on-chip meander monopole antenna resonating at 16 GHz on a silicon photonic chip. The inter-chip communication is demonstrated with maximum transmission coefficient value of -18.2 dB.

articleTitle: Characterization of a terahertz pulse train generation and modulation source
abstract: We demonstrate a new technique for the generation and active modulation of a terahertz (THz) pulse train using the combination of an echelon mirror that generates the optical beam train, a digital micromirror device (DMD) that modulates the optical beam train and a spintronic terahertz emitter (STE).

articleTitle: Arrayed Waveguide Grating Reconfigurable Optical Cross Connect Router
abstract: In this work we present a reconfigurable optical arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) cross connect router based on controlling the phase in the arrayed waveguide region by introducing small excessive delay to this region. This can be handy in the design of AWG devices that serves as an optical cross connect. The introduced delay is the outcome of varying the phase in the different arrayed waveguides between the two free propagation regions (FPR) using a thermo-optic or electrooptic modulator. The arrayed waveguides used in this design employed a reverse biased single mode PN-Junction waveguides (PNJW) fabricated on silicon on insulator (SOI) substrate. The applied voltage on the PNJW controls the phase delay and consequently controls the outputs from the second free propagation regions (FPR2). Simulation is carried out for the structure as individual blocks using commercial software lumerical INTERCONNECT. The results for switching of the optical signal from one port to another one has been achieved.

articleTitle: InGaN nanostructures supported rhodium nanoclusters for green syngas production from CO2 and H2O powered by sunlight
abstract: Solar-powered syngas production via methane steam reforming presents a revolutionary strategy for producing transportable liquid fuel and chemical commodities. Simultaneous activation of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O is the key for achieving high performance solar-fuel production such as syngas. However, it has remained challenging to efficiently reform CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. In this work, one-dimensional nanostructured InGaN-supported Rh species vertically aligned is assembled for green syngas production with the only inputs of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, and sunlight. On the basis of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, in combination with state-of-the-art in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier-transform spectroscopy and electron magnetic resonance spectroscopy characterization, it is revealed that that the wurtzite GaN is synergistic with ultrafine Rh nanoparticles (NPs) for deforming the symmetrical tetrahedral configuration of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and for dissociating the O-H bond of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O (Fig. 1). Consequently, the assembled architecture of Rh NPs/GaN NWs illustrates exceptional syngas activity of 5.0 mol•g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cat</inf>-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>•h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, with a benchmarking turnover frequency of 3200 mol CO+H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> per mol Rh species per hour. It I s worthwhile mentioning that engineering the components of this rational architecture, the ratio of CO/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> can be flexibly varied from 1.2 to 2.3 for meeting the practical demand of high-value downstream products.

articleTitle: Minimally invasive medical diagnosis through Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) coupled with machine learning
abstract: Untargeted spectroscopic methods allow interrogating biomedical samples without prior hypotheses about specific pathways, and therefore they are a powerful diagnostic tool for poorly understood or initially asymptomatic diseases. In this work, we analyzed micro- drops of biological fluids from patients and animal models with Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) and coupled the spectra with supervised classification algorithms to distinguish healthy and diseased individuals. LIBS is the optical emission spectroscopy of laser-induced plasmas, and it can provide the elemental fingerprinting of a wide variety of samples [1]. In [2], we designed a voting algorithm based on the use of LIBS difference spectra, that we employed as a data-pretreatment and feature-selection method to couple with Quadratic Discriminant Analysis for Alzheimer’s Disease diagnosis in living patients.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband silicon beam-splitter based on subwavelength metamaterials
abstract: We propose an ultra-broadband and fabrication-tolerant symmetric Y–junction leveraging subwavelength metamaterials. A comprehensive experimental study over a 260 nm bandwidth (1420–1680 nm) shows TE0 excess loss below 0.3 dB. Low losses are maintained even in the presence of fabrication deviations of ±10 nm. Our power splitter also exhibits excess loss lower than 1 dB for the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> mode within 1475–1575 nm.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Pulses from All-Fiber Mamyshev Oscillators
abstract: We describe the principle of operation of Mamyshev oscillators that produce powerful femtosecond pulses. We present our results obtained with all-fiber Mamyshev oscillators terminated by fiber Bragg gratings. Such sources offer a broad range of possibilities in terms of pulse energy and repetition rate.

articleTitle: On-Chip Virus Sensing Using Silicon Nitride Waveguide
abstract: Here we study the silicon nitride waveguide platform for virus sensing. Our study cover different wavelengths from the visible to the mid-infrared range where the silicon nitride is transparent. At each wavelength we do sensitivity analysis to get the optimum waveguide dimensions for virus detection. Analysis show that operating at lower wavelengths results in higher sensitivities. The optimized waveguides can work for different viruses. Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) sensors based on the optimized waveguides are designed showing sensitivity as high as 5573 nm/RIU.

articleTitle: Recent Progress on Short-wavelength-emitting AlGaN Nanowire Deep UV LEDs
abstract: In this work, we report recent progress on short-wavelength-emitting aluminum gallium nitride (AlGaN) nanowire deep ultraviolet (UV) light emitting diodes (LEDs) with polarization enhanced tunnel junction (TJ) and p-layer.

articleTitle: LWIR FSO Receivers using Orientation Patterned Semiconductors
abstract: A novel sum frequency generation (SFG) intracavity structure for detecting LWIR light via conversion to the SWIR band is presented. Simulation results using the coupled nonlinear wave equations and a spatially dependent cavity model show that microwatt level power can be generated from milliwatt level sources. Use of orientation-patterned semiconductors for the LWIR as the nonlinear medium is also discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the operation of a Non-Line-of-Sight wireless network cluster operating at the solar-blind part of the UV-C wavelength band
abstract: The implementation aspects and the performance evaluation of a Non-Line-of-Sight wireless network operating at 265 nm for covering short distances at low rates are presented.

Author Keywords: Non-Line-of-Sight wireless network in UV-C band
Medium Access Control Protocol for NLOS network

articleTitle: Adiabatic inversion scheme for solid-state emitters using frequency-swept, spectrally-modified pulses
abstract: Adiabatic control via spectrally-modified pulses is demonstrated as a pumping scheme for solid-state emitters that enables high-fidelity inversion together with spectral isolation of scattered pump light from the emitted photon stream. This scheme paves the way for on-demand single photon sources with simultaneous high single photon purity, indistinguishability and brightness.

articleTitle: Fully Integrated SiN/SOI (De)Multiplexer for the O-band
abstract: We present the experimental demonstration of a silicon nitride (de)multiplexer fully integrated with a thick silicon-on-insulator platform for coarse wavelength division multiplexing applications in the O-band.

articleTitle: Broadband multimode waveguide bend in the SOI platform
abstract: In this paper, we present a design and experimental demonstration of a 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> broadband multimode waveguide bend that supports the propagation of multiple modes on a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform. In order to achieve efficient mode multiplexing, we utilize trapezoidal-shaped subwavelength grating (SWG) segments, which are bridged by adiabatically tapered radial strips to form a gradient curvature bend. Using a 220 nm SOI wafer, our unique design of the multimode bend has a radius of 10 μm and only requires a single full etch step. We report successful experimental demonstration of a multimode waveguide bend that supports at least 4 modes, across a broad bandwidth of 100 nm, centered at 1550 nm. This work offers a promising potential for broadband mode-division multiplexers.

articleTitle: Prototyping of Silicon Nitride Photonic Integrated Circuits using Electron Beam Lithography
abstract: We describe a rapid prototyping process for silicon nitride photonic integrated circuits. The prototyping platform is based on direct-write electron beam lithography technology and provides a route toward the rapid fabrication of chip-based passive and thermo-optic active photonic devices with critical resolution down to 100 nm.

articleTitle: Improving Topological Confinement with Engineered Element Geometry
abstract: We show that the confinement of topological systems based on dielectric pillar lattices can be improved by morphing individual pillars to a teardrop shape, offering new building blocks for designing more compact optical circuits under the same platform.

articleTitle: Superradiance from spectrally tailored absorption lines in a cavity
abstract: Superradiance is a coherent emission phenomenon from an ensemble of emitters that share a collective excitation, and has potential applications in quantum metrology, quantum communication, and quantum computing. We demonstrate superradiant emission in a thulium-doped yttrium aluminium garnet (Tm:YAG) crystal, whose input and output faces are reflection coated to form a cavity that satisfies the impedance matching condition for light on resonance with the Tm transition line. This implementation allows us to observe superradiant emission in the low optical depth regime (OD approx. 1). We engineer the characteristic decay of the superradiant emission by tailoring the inhomogeneously broadened spectrum of Tm:YAG into absorption lines with different shapes, depths, and widths, and perform simulations over a wide range of parameters. We extend this investigation and discuss the possibility of a broadband quantum memory based on superradiance for long-distance quantum networks.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance Comparison of Silicon Ring-based WDM and MDM Multiplexers
abstract: We investigated the thermal behavior of wavelength and mode silicon ring-based multiplexers through simulations and found that the performance of mode multiplexers is more sensitive to temperature.

articleTitle: Yb:YAG laser pumped at 946 nm
abstract: High power continuous-wave Yb:YAG laser pumped by a compact Nd:YAG laser at 946 nm is reported. The laser generated maximum output power of 4.37 W at an absorbed pump power of 6.22 W with a slope efficiency of 70%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first implementation of Yb:YAG laser pumped by a Nd:YAG laser at 946 nm.

articleTitle: Theory of high order Raman generation with chirped pulses
abstract: High order Raman generation produces high intensity ultrashort laser pulses through the efficient conversion of energy to a number of frequencies separated by the Raman frequency of the medium. Experimentally, when the Raman medium is excited with short chirped laser pulses, the spectra of each Raman order have a single sideband shifted to a lower frequency. These red-shifted sidebands are not explained by the current continuous wave theory for high order Raman generation. We derive the terms of the spectrum when linearly chirped Gaussian pulses are used in high order Raman generation.

articleTitle: In-band pumped CW Nd:YAP laser
abstract: We report on continuous-wave Nd:YAP laser with in-band diode pumping around 910 nm. The laser produced an average output power of 1.15 W at 1079 nm.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystals in Quantum Optics: Current Experiments, Applications and Future Prospects
abstract: A review will be presented on using liquid crystal properties of molecular alignment and self-assembly into photonic bandgap structures in quantum and nano-photonics. Advances in transparent planar optics using modulation of the geometrical (Pancharatnam-Berry) phase will be outlined. The author’s results on single-photon sources with definite polarizations and collaborative research on using liquid crystals for modeling quantum mechanical tunneling phenomena will be overviewed. Future prospects of patterned liquid crystals and topological defects in these materials will be discussed.

articleTitle: Nd:YAG laser at 946 nm with improved beam quality
abstract: Continuous-wave Nd:YAG laser operating at 946 nm with improved beam quality is presented. We obtained the maximum output power of 9.98 W at an incident pump power of 31 W. The beam quality factor M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was ~5. To the best of our knowledge, this is the highest output power generated at 946 nm from bulk Nd:YAG crystals with such a beam quality.

articleTitle: Generation of indistinguishable photons using a hybrid III-V nanowire–SiN photonic circuit platform
abstract: Single photons are required in many applications involving quantum information processing. Integrating such sources on chip offers enhanced stability, miniaturization, and scalability. We employ a "pick and place" technique to integrate III-V nanowire-based single-photon sources with on-chip photonic circuitry. This approach provides for efficient coupling of the quantum light generated in a photonic nanowire to a SiN-based photonic integrated circuit. We have previously demonstrated that such devices can efficiently generate single photons on chip. Here we study the potential for generating indistinguishable photons from such sources. We demonstrate post-selected two-photon interference visibilities of up to 70% between sequential photons emitted from the same quantum dot when excited above-band. These findings show that the proposed approach offers a viable route for the integration of a stable source of indistinguishable photons on chip.

articleTitle: Optimizing UV LED emission characteristics for an efficient module design
abstract: Optimization of emission characteristics for UV LEDs using optics can lead to a reduction in overall system costs. Application-specific optical design with beam shaping can reduce thermal budgets, decrease exposure times, and offer higher returns for UV LEDs. We present results in optical performance improvement of UV LED modules through the use of UV-transparent materials and secondary optics.

articleTitle: Polarity Control of Nanowire-template-assisted AlN Epilayers on Si by Molecular Beam Epitaxy
abstract: In this paper, we report the polarity control of AlN epilayers on Si. Such AlN epilayers are grown by molecular beam epitaxy, assisted by a nanowire template. The use of N-rich and Al-rich conditions leads to N-polar and Al-polar AlN epilayers, respectively, in spite that the nanowire template is N-polar.

articleTitle: Radiative Cooling of a Silicon Nitride Nanomechanical Resonator
abstract: Radiative cooling allows for the temperature of an object to diminish below ambient temperature by coupling it with the coldness of outer space via thermal radiation. Creating local thermal gradients on-chip with this phenomenon could potentially enable microscale energy conversion devices running on ambient heat. Here, we demonstrate localized radiative cooling of an on-chip silicon nitride membrane by up to 6.4 K at night, and 5.4 K during the day, under direct sunlight. This is in agreement with our theoretical model, which predicts a temperature drop of 5 K - 9 K for our experimental parameters, and a maximal drop of 15 K in ideal field of view and atmospheric conditions.

articleTitle: Short-wavelength Surface-emitting Vertical Semiconductor UV LEDs with Graphene Electrode
abstract: This work demonstrates surface-emitting vertical AlGaN nanowire deep ultraviolet light-emitting diodes down to 240 nm with transferred graphene as the top electrode.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Yb:CALGO laser with a White cell
abstract: A femtosecond laser operating at 13.85 MHz repetition rate using a White cell was demonstrated. By using a 15% output coupler, 73 fs pulses with 750 mW of output power at 21 W of incident pump power were obtained. The calculated pulse energy was 54 nJ and the corresponding peak power was 744 kW.

articleTitle: Terahertz Extended Kalman Filtering Method
abstract: Terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is a well-established spectroscopy technique that can investigate modes of molecules, particularly in vapour. However, maximum detectable absorption is often low and depends on the dynamic range of the THz-TDS system and the thickness of the sample. With the burden of low dynamic range in realistic environmental settings, THz-TDS systems often are infeasible to implement [1] . This is exacerbated when THz-TDS is applied to highly absorptive samples such as occurs in microfluidics [2] , which is a favourable application for THz-TDS [1] .

articleTitle: Heterogeneously integrated III-V/Si Tunable lasers
abstract: In this work we will review our latest advancements on the development of widely tunable lasers using an heterogeneous integrated technology that combines an InP-based photonic platform containing Al-based multiple quantum wells with silicon photonic integrated circuits defined on a SOI platform.

articleTitle: Silicon photonics: advanced metamaterials and sensors
abstract: Silicon photonics is an enabling platform for high-speed optical communications and sensing. Here we review some recent advances in building devices with breakthrough performance using subwavelength metamaterials as well as advanced sensing systems leveraging telecom techniques.

articleTitle: Wavelength-agnostic Denoising of Optical Signals
abstract: We demonstrate the self-tracking ability of Talbot-based denoising amplification by simultaneously denoising multiple wavelength-multiplexed data signals, without any requirement for stabilization or alignment.

articleTitle: All-fiber denoising sampling of GHz-bandwidth temporal optical waveforms
abstract: We demonstrate denoising temporal sampling of arbitrary waveforms with GHz-bandwidths through an all-fiber Talbot-based amplification scheme.

articleTitle: Volumetric Observation of Microwave Resonances in Grape-sized Aqueous Spheroids
abstract: New evidence for morphology dependent resonances in irradiated hydrogel spheres at microwave oven frequencies is provided via volumetric calorimetry. The size-dependent effect is closely corroborated with FEM simulation.

articleTitle: Broadband and high-sensitivity time-resolved THz system using grating-assisted noncollinear phase matching
abstract: We demonstrate a broadband and high-sensitivity terahertz (THz) time-resolved system relying on THz generation and detection in thick nonlinear crystals. A phase grating etched at the front surface of a 2 mm thick GaP crystal enables noncollinear phase matching between a diffracted near-infrared pulse and a non-diffracted THz pulse. Our system features a 6 THz bandwidth, similar to the one obtained with a standard configuration relying on 0.2 mm thick GaP crystals, but provides a larger spectral peak intensity, up to a factor of 400, due to an increased nonlinear interaction length.

articleTitle: Compressed ultrahigh-speed photography enabled by a snapshot-to-video autoencoder
abstract: Ultrahigh-speed optical imaging of transient scenes is indispensable in numerous areas of study, however, existing techniques, e.g., compressed optical-streaking ultrahigh-speed photography (COSUP), are limited by the long processing time and unstable image quality in existing analytical-modeling-based video reconstruction. To address these limitations, we have developed a snapshot-to-video autoencoder (S2V-AE)—a new neural network that maps a compressively recorded 2D image to a movie. The S2V-AE enables the development of single-shot machine-learning assisted real-time (SMART) COSUP, which features a reconstruction time of 60 ms and a large sequence depth of 100 frames. SMART-COSUP is applied to wide-field multipleparticle tracking at 20 thousand frames-per-second (kfps).

articleTitle: Distributed Bragg Reflector Cavities on Tellurium Oxide-Coated Silicon Nitride Waveguides
abstract: We report on the design and characterization of Bragg grating-based cavities on silicon nitride waveguides. The potential of such devices on achieving on-chip lasers with rare-earth-doped tellurium oxide coatings is discussed.

articleTitle: Optimized Polarization-Independent, Wide-Band Metamaterial Perfect Absorber for Infrared Energy Harvesting
abstract: We present a gradient-based optimization approach to design a metamaterial perfect absorber (MPA) operating at infrared (IR) wavelengths, specifically around 10.6 μm. The optimal design supports a wide-band absorptivity and its symmetry results in a polarization-insensitive operation. The proposed MPA is composed of a split-ring resonator concentric with crossed-ellipses. This MPA represents the top metallic layer of a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) structure. Magnetic polaritons (MP) at 10 μm leads to a wide reception-angle performance. The ease of forming thin insulator layers inside the gaps of the proposed MPA enables building an IR-energy harvester element similar to the rectenna’s operation. Also, the strong electric field enhancement at these gaps improves the performance of MIM rectifiers. Moreover, the coupling between these MPAs and MIM rectifiers is studied and shows that our proposed design is a good candidate for energy harvest application with capability of scaling the design to different wavelengths.

articleTitle: Airy Beams on Incoherent Background
abstract: We present a class of diffraction-free partially coherent beams, each member of which comprises a finite-power, non-accelerating Airy bump residing on a statistically homogeneous, Gaussian-correlated background. We examine free-space propagation of soft apertured realizations of the proposed beams and show that their evolution is governed by two spatial scales: the coherence width of the background and the aperture size. A relative magnitude of these factors determines the practical range of propagation distances over which the novel beams can withstand diffraction.

articleTitle: Localized Facet Joule Heating of Mid-infrared Quantum Cascade Lasers
abstract: The self-heating or so-called joule-heating effect is detrimental for mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers (MIR QCLs), especially when a high-power electrical current is injected. In this abstract, strong localized heat confinement is observed on the laser facet within a small region between the electroplated gold (EP-Au) layer and the air interface located on the top of the ridge waveguide by employing spatially resolved time-domain thermoreflectance (SR-TDTR) microscopy. In addition, hot spots are clearly observed on this EP-Au layer close to the laser facet due to the imperfect facet cleaving. These results shed light on the significance and improvement of the MIR QCLs thermal management.

articleTitle: Polychromatic-DHM automation: towards quasi-speckle-free quantitative phase imaging of cell dynamics
abstract: We propose an automatized polychromatic digital holographic microscope (P-DHM) to achieve quasi-speckle-free quantitative phase imaging (QPI) with a faster and more robust strategy.

articleTitle: High Pulse-to-Pulse Stability High Power Femtosecond Yb-doped Fiber Laser
abstract: We present high pulse-to-pulse (P2P) stability of Ytterbium-doped (YDF) pulsed fiber laser. The P2P fluctuation of 2.4 percent for seed and 3.4 percent after grating compressor is achieved. Ultra-stable mode-locking with repetition rate of 42MHz is generated by utilizing a narrow bandwidth fiber Bragg grating (FBG) in the seed with 0.2nm bandwidth. The spectrum is broadened in the amplifier to about 20nm due to self-phase modulation (SPM) while the output average power is above 7W. The pulse is then compressed to about 200fs by a pair of transmission grating.

articleTitle: Photonic Millimeter-Wave-over-Fiber MIMO Wireless System Based on a QDash Laser
abstract: In this paper, we experimentally demonstrate a photonic-assisted millimeter-wave-over-fiber (MMWoF) 2×2 MIMO wireless transmission system employing a low noise quantum dash (QDash) dual-wavelength DFB laser. The 2×2 MIMO structure is realized through optical polarization multiplexing and remote heterodyning of a single optical source together with cross-polarization configuration of two pairs of antennas to avoid interference at the receiver reducing system complexity. The demonstration includes real-time transmission and detection of wideband 2-GBaud 16-QAM MMW wireless signals at the V-band in a 2×2 MIMO configuration over 2-m wireless distance through 10-km single mode fiber (SMF). This results in doubling the system data capacity to 16-Gb/s. The system performance is evaluated exhibiting error vector magnitude (EVM) well below the standard requirements of 12.5%.

articleTitle: Terahertz metasurface based on additive manufacturing technology
abstract: We compare and analyze terahertz (THz) metasurfaces fabricated using two distinct additive manufacturing (AM) technologies, i.e., printable electronics (PE) and three-dimensional (3D) printing. With terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS), the performance of these devices was investigated. Both samples’ transmission characteristics were consistent with simulation results, demonstrating the effectiveness of the manufacturing technique and that they can be widely used for bandpass filtering applications at a low cost.

articleTitle: Low-power pulse conversion through efficient shock-front formation in monolithic liquid-core optical fibres
abstract: We demonstrate numerically and experimentally efficient shock-front formation in all-spliced liquid-core fibers, paving the way to coherent, gaussian pulse compression in the normal dispersion regime and at very low pulse energies.

articleTitle: 4 × 75 Gbit/s WDM PAM-8 Transmission Over 25 km for Future Optical Access Communications
abstract: We demonstrate 300 Gbit/s PAM-8 transmissions over a 25 km single-mode fiber for the next-generation optical access networks. Bit error ratios below 3.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>were obtained for received power as low as -7 dBm.

articleTitle: UV-driven Multidimensional Solitary States in Hollow Core Fiber
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the formation of multidimensional solitary states (MDSS) in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O-filled hollow-core fiber (HCF), driven by ultraviolet (UV) pulses.

articleTitle: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy of 3D Printed Materials
abstract: Terahertz (THz) photons reside within the frequency range of 100 GHz to 10 THz, corresponding to a wavelength range of 30 µm to 3000 µm—formally known as the THz gap [1] . Modern advancements in the generation and detection of terahertz photons, utilizing photo-conductive antennas and electro-optic detectors, have overcome the THz gap in the electromagnetic spectrum. This has prompted the incorporation of THz photons into traditional spectroscopic and imaging techniques.

articleTitle: Coupling efficiency of III-nitride quantum dot emissions to ridge waveguides in a quantum photonic integrated device
abstract: III-nitride quantum dots (QD) based single photon emitters are promising for a broad range of quantum photonic applications including secure quantum communication, quantum metrology and quantum computing. III-nitride QDs exhibit wide and tunable energy bandgap, therefore suitable for high temperature operations over a wide spectral range for on demand single photon and entangled photon pairs. The III-nitride nanophotonic waveguides are also preferred due to the extremely low optical losses. An efficient coupling of the quantum dot emissions to the photonic waveguides will play a crucial role towards realizing all nitride quantum photonic integrated circuits (QPIC) allowing the integration of quantum emitters in conventional nanophotonic devices.

articleTitle: Improved Slope Efficiency of InAs/InP Quantum Dash Mode-Locked Lasers
abstract: This paper presents the performance of InAs/InP quantum dash (QDash) mode-locked lasers with different number of QDash layers. Decreasing the number of QDash layers leads to a markedly reduced threshold and improved slope efficiency. This provides insight toward the application of QDash mode-locked laser to the field of optical transmission for all-optical networks.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity reduction in a fiber interferometer interrogated by a wavelength sweeping diode laser
abstract: The sensing signal generated in fiber interferometers interrogated by a wavelength sweeping laser normally presents a certain degree of nonlinearity, which degrades the performance of fiber sensors. In this work, we report a method to reduce this effect by using a small section of the scanning period for sensing purpose, reducing in this way the non-linearity effect accumulated along the whole scanning period. The proposed method is used for refractive index measurement, and improves the resolution of the system from 3 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> to 2 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>; it also makes the sensor insensitive to temperature. To prove the improvement in the system performance, the thermo-optic coefficients of liquid samples were measured. The proposed method can be implemented in any other interferometric sensor interrogated by a wavelength sweeping laser.

articleTitle: Probing Micron-sized Objects with Photoacoustic Sensing: Theory and Applications
abstract: The covid-19 respiratory illness caused by the rapid spread of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) resulted in a worldwide pandemic over the past two years. Despite vaccinations and preventative screening methods, covid-19 remains a global issue in part due to high contagiousness and airborne transmission via droplet aerosolization. Current screening methods lack sensitivity or have a slow response time. In this study, we investigate an air-based photoacoustic spectroscopy method to rapidly detect viral RNA within aerosolized droplets.

articleTitle: Predicting Dielectric Waveguides Characteristics Using Deep Learning
abstract: We propose an unsupervised deep learning model based on physics-informed neural network (PINNS) to find the effective refractive index of a slab waveguide. The model accuracy could reach 99% within a time range from 60 to 120 seconds for symmetric and anti-symmetric waveguide. The results show the success of the introduced method in solving fail cases of the compared methods.

articleTitle: Multi-diffraction-order plasmonic lattice resonances
abstract: We demonstrate excitation of ultra-high-Q multi-diffraction-order lattice resonances covering the infrared and visible optical spectrum inside a plasmonic metasurface-integrated dielectric transparent thin film.

articleTitle: AlGaN Epilayers on Si Substrate with High Internal Quantum Efficiency
abstract: In this paper, we report the molecular beam epitaxial growth of AlGaN epilayers on Si substrate with high internal quantum efficiency.

articleTitle: Optical manipulation of biological objects on azobenzene-containing systems
abstract: Cells interact with a chemical and mechanical environment that influences their adaptive response and conditions the physiology and pathophysiology of the tissues. Much effort is being made to reconstruct simple systems in order to study the reciprocal influences of tissues and their environment, as well as to measure the consequences of environmental disturbances on cells. Specific tools are required for the in-vivo, real-time manipulation of the cellular environment’s mechanical properties and for the measurement of the resulting local and collective cellular biomechanical responses. One innovative solution is the use of photoactive systems such as azobenzene-containing polymer materials (azopolymers), whose microstructure and mechanical optical and surface properties can be modulated in time and space by light. Here we show that azopolymer bio-substrates can be used to optically control and study the cellular response of mouse fibroblasts and to single out different classes of cellular responses that might specifically depend on the photo-induced mechanical modification of the environment surrounding the cellular focal adhesions.

articleTitle: Systemic comparison of dielectric and plasmonic biosensors on a silicon photonics platform
abstract: Plasmonic and dielectric based waveguides are widely used for biosensing applications. However, the use of different sensing architectures and platforms hinders the fair comparison of their respective figures of merit. In this paper, plasmonic and dielectric-based photonic waveguide biosensors are compared in terms of attainable limit of detection, using in both cases a coherent-readout interferometric architecture and the same commercial manufacturing platform.

articleTitle: Coherent Transmission Over Ten Tbit/s Using an InAs/InP Quantum Dot Mode-Locked Laser
abstract: This paper presents results from an InAs/InP quantum dot (QDot) C-band passively mode-locked laser (MLL) for frequency comb generation. By using this single-section QDot-MLL we demonstrate an aggregate line rate of over ten Tbit/s 16QAM data transmission capacity for both back-to-back (B2B) and over 100-km of standard single mode fiber (SSMF). This finding highlights the viability for InAs/InP QDot lasers to be used as a low-cost optical source for large-scale networks.

articleTitle: Infrared Photon-Pair Generation in a Liquid-Filled Microstructured Optical Fiber
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the generation of frequency non-degenerate correlated photon pairs with more than 1µm spectral distance in a liquid-core microstructured optical fiber via four-wave mixing.

articleTitle: Silicon-germanium photodetectors for energy-aware chip-scale communications
abstract: We report on recent advances in silicon-germanium-silicon photodetectors with lateral p-i-n hetero-junctions. They are fast, sensitive and consume only a few fJ/bit. Such optical photodetectors hold much promises for future on-chip communications.

articleTitle: Single-shot phosphorescence lifetime imaging thermometry for wide-field temperature sensing
abstract: Photoluminescence lifetime imaging of upconverting nanoparticles (UCNPs) is useful for optical thermometry but has not yet been implemented in wide-field temperature sensing in a single exposure. To overcome this limitation, we have developed single-shot photoluminescence lifetime imaging thermometry (SPLIT). Using the core/shell structured UCNPs as the temperature indicators, we apply SPLIT to wide-field temperature mapping of a dynamic biological sample at video rate.

articleTitle: Photonic Image Rejection Filter for Optical Beamforming Network
abstract: We have designed an integrated photonic image rejection filter for use in an optical beamforming network. Ring resonator-based image rejection topology is adapted to achieve a maximally flat passband transmission and a low delay dispersion simultaneously. Additionally, a pseudo elliptic image rejection filter is designed with a group delay ripple of < 1 ps and a suppression of more than 35 dB to demonstrate its viability in an optical beamforming network.

articleTitle: Loop-Terminated Mach-Zehnder Interferometer Silicon-Organic Hybrid Modulator
abstract: In this work we present a silicon-organic hybrid loop-terminated Mach-Zehnder interferometer (LT-MZI) modulator utilizing slot waveguides in a push-pull configuration. The slots are filled with electro-optic polymer (EOP) that exhibits Pockel’s effect. This design allow for compact modulator with low energy consumption and high operating speed. The modulator is based on the widespread silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technology. Our modulator can reach up to 100 GHz frequency with femtojoule energy consumption. Finite difference time domain (FDTD) solver shows that our modulator can reach extinction ratio (ER) as high as 40 dB at 1.55 µm wavelength with only 1.15 dB insertion loss (IL).

articleTitle: Development of a CW tunable Yb:YLF laser
abstract: High power continuous-wave operation of a diode-pumped Yb:YLF laser was investigated. The laser generated 8.4 W of output power for 20 W of incident pump power. The wavelength tuning range of the laser was also measured by using a birefringent filter plate and laser operation from 1025 nm to 1073 nm was obtained at room temperature. These results indicate good potential for generation of high power ultrashort pulses based on Yb:YLF crystal.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Hot Carriers and Their Applications
abstract: Under optical illumination, plasmonic nanostructures become efficient generators of energetic (hot) carriers. We discuss nanoscale structures that support surface plasmons and exploit hot carriers for optoelectronic and catalysis applications.

articleTitle: Application Specific Interface to Control and Calibrate Programmable Photonic Integrated Circuits
abstract: A custom in-house designed interface to provide accurate driving voltage for a 4 × 4 Mach-Zehnder interferometer based photonic processor is presented providing the required tool to assess and calibrate both electrical and optical crosstalk.

articleTitle: Towards Large-Scale Silicon Photonic Programmable Optical Processors for Machine Learning and Optical Quantum Computing
abstract: We discuss the progress made towards large-scale programmable optical processors on Silicon Photonics for ultrafast and energy efficient computing.

articleTitle: Double-pulse Model for the Study of Red-shifted Spectrum in Multi-frequency Raman Generation
abstract: Pumped by two frequency chirped pulses in the transient regime, the anti-Stokes orders from multi-frequency Raman Generation are spectrally broadened on the lower frequency side, causing each of the orders to have a broader spectrum with double-peak pattern. In this letter, a double-pulse model is introduced to analyze the measured spectrograms. We think the red-shifted spectrum comes from the linear Raman scattering between manifolds in the two-photon dressed states.

articleTitle: Breaking the transverse-magnetic polarized light emission bottleneck of AlGaN LED using nano-patterned substrates and Al reflector
abstract: Ultraviolet light-emitting diodes based on Al-rich AlGaN semiconductors operating in the 210 nm-280 nm have drawn significant interest for many critical applications, including water purification, disinfection of air and surface as preventive measures of SARS COV-2, sterilization, etc. However, for the above-mentioned applications, the current technology still relies on toxic and inefficient mercury-based UV lamps. Driven by the immense need for an efficient, mercury-free, compact alternative technology, future water purification and disinfection technologies require the development of high-efficiency UV-C light-emitting diodes. To date, the external quantum efficiency (EQE) in AlGaN quantum well (QW) UV-LED heterostructures has been severely limited due to several factors including large densities of defects/dislocations, extremely low light extraction efficiency (LEE) of dominant transverse magnetic (TM) light, absorptive p -GaN contact, and total internal reflection (TIR).
